text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The government announces plans to tighten next year's budget in line with economic reform programme. The budget is projected to be $1.1bn. Of that, the state expects $1bn will come from indirect taxation, five million from direct taxes and around 70 million from international financial institutions. Inflation is projected at two percent and GDP growth at five percent.
- Thirteen commercial banks and seven savings banks establoish a fund for ensuring savings deposits in Macedonia.
- The opposition coalition's candidate Risto Penov officialy declared mayor of Skopje.
- The opposition Democratic Party accuses the rulling Social Democratic Alliance (SDAM) of manipulating results of the local elections.

- The largest opposition party, the Internal Macedonian Revolutionary Organisation, demands the Macedonian press recognise the opposition coalition's victory in local elections. The party leader Ljucpo Georgievski warns the government "not to provoke the Serbian scenario in Macedonia by manipulating the votes of the citizens".

- The ethnic Albanian Party for Democratic Prosperity (PDP), which is in coaltion with the rulling SDAM, declares victory over its rivals, the Party for Democratic Prosperity of Albanians (PDP-A) in western regions of Macedonia. The party says it has 13 mayors to the PDP-A's four. The two parties are to contest a re-run of the vote in Tetovo, repeated because of irregularities. -- Mircela Casule, Skopje newsroom +389 91 201196
